sections.h2: Ways to sell in West Bend
sections.html:
You have three ways to sell in West Bend: hire an agent, go without one, or take a cash buyer's offer. At the finish, every one of them needs a deed on record with Washington County and a transfer return filed with the state.

The house's condition and your calendar settle the choice.

  • An agent listing works for a house in good repair, if you can sit through showings, an inspection and a buyer's loan approval.
  • Going alone saves the agent's fee, though pricing, paperwork and negotiating land on you.
  • A cash offer is for a house that needs work, a West Bend property you inherited, or a sale where timing outranks the last dollar.

Put each offer's terms on paper and compare the net after the transfer fee, taxes owed and repairs.

West Bend is the Washington County seat, in the Milwaukee metropolitan area, with an estimated 32,268 residents in 2025, up from 31,752 at the 2020 census. Homes are valued below the county median, and a higher share of households rent. A lot of houses went up during the postwar growth, which is why buyers focus on the roof, furnace and basement.

These are medians for the whole city, so a particular street can sit well above or below them.

Cold, snowy winters put the heating system and roof at the top of a buyer's list. West Bend sits in the Kettle Moraine region, where glaciers left kettles and hills, and hilly ground can send runoff toward a foundation. Keep a note of any grading or drainage work. Storm damage history is also a normal question from buyers.

Before you list, gather paperwork for these items:

  • Roof, siding and window replacement dates, with the City permit if one was pulled.
  • Furnace and air conditioner age and service records.
  • Any basement water repair, sump pump work or insurance claim.

Buyers ask about the West Bend School District and the route to Milwaukee. West Bend East and West High Schools will consolidate into a single West Bend High School for the 2027-2028 school year. For commuting, US 45 runs as a freeway bypass west of downtown, with Wisconsin 33 and Wisconsin 144 also serving the city. The Washington County Commuter Express bus to Milwaukee ended in 2023, so most commuters drive, and the average trip to work is 25.9 minutes.

sections.h2: Which City of West Bend permits matter before you sell?
sections.html:
Work done without a permit can slow a sale, so check your permit history with the City of West Bend Building Inspection office at (262) 335-5140. Permits must be obtained before any building activity begins, and inspections are scheduled within 24 to 48 hours of a request.

A permit is required for each of these:

  • Finishing a basement, remodeling living space, adding a dormer, an addition or a three-season room.
  • Adding or replacing a deck or porch.
  • Replacing roofing or siding.
  • Installing a shed, fence, driveway or swimming pool.
  • Replacing a furnace or air conditioner.

Detached garages and other accessory structures are capped at 720 square feet in total, and a detached garage at 18 feet in height. The owner and occupant of a single-family home may do their own electrical and plumbing work with a permit. Duplex and condo owners may not, and no homeowner may work on the electrical service to the home or on a pool or spa. Suspect a previous owner skipped a permit? Ask the office how to close it out before an inspector for the buyer discovers it.

sections.h2: Recording a deed in Washington County
sections.html:
Recording a deed costs $30 for most documents under Wis. Stat. 59.43(2)(ag). State law adds a seller-paid transfer fee of 30 cents for each $100 of value under Wis. Stat. 77.22(1), which is $3 per $1,000.

The fee is collected as the deed comes in, and the deed must carry a completed real estate transfer return that was filed online with the Department of Revenue. For questions, call the register of deeds at 262-335-4320.

A few transfers owe nothing. Wis. Stat. 77.25 lists them, and the ones homeowners meet most often are inheritance transfers, deeds in lieu of foreclosure, gifts within a family line for little or no payment, and any transfer of real estate worth $1,000 or less.

Washington County offers a free service called LandNotification, which sends an email when a document is recorded under a name or parcel you pick. Recording alone does not transfer ownership, and the alert helps you spot a bogus filing early.

sections.h2: How property taxes are handled when a West Bend house sells
sections.html:
Property tax on a West Bend house is billed in arrears and is usually prorated between buyer and seller at closing. Bills go out by the third Monday in December. Wis. Stat. 74.11 splits real property tax into two equal installments, January 31 and July 31, except that a bill under $100 is due whole by January 31.

If the first installment has not arrived within five working days after January 31, the entire unpaid balance becomes delinquent on February 1. An owner who is behind can ask the Washington County treasurer for the balance with interest, and the title company can then pay it out of the proceeds.

Owners who live in the house may see the lottery and gaming credit on the bill. That credit stays with the property at sale, so count it when taxes are prorated. A buyer who will live there files a new application.

Buyers in West Bend usually ask for permit history, service records and any record of water in the basement. Keep them together in one folder before the first showing. If you handled electrical or plumbing work yourself, make sure the permit was pulled, since the city allows owner work only with one.

Add the deed that put you on title and a recent tax bill. As offers arrive, have each buyer name a closing date, say who pays for title and recording, and tell you whether a loan is involved. A cash buyer purchases as-is, which can remove the repair list, but the written terms still matter.

faqs.q: How is the transfer fee figured on a West Bend sale?
faqs.a: Multiply the sale price by 0.30 percent. The rate is 30 cents per $100 of value, counting any leftover fraction of $100. The register of deeds takes it when the deed is submitted.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer fee in West Bend?
faqs.a: The seller pays it. Wis. Stat. 77.22(1) puts the fee on the grantor, and it is collected by Washington County's register of deeds when the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Can I do my own electrical or plumbing work on my West Bend house?
faqs.a: Yes, as the owner-occupant of a single-family home, and a permit is still required. Duplex and condo owners may not do their own work, and no homeowner may touch the electrical service or work on a swimming pool or spa.

faqs.q: Does the lottery credit go to the buyer of my West Bend house?
faqs.a: It stays with the property, comes off the next tax bill, and should be counted in the proration. A buyer who plans to live there files again.

faqs.q: How can I watch for deed fraud on my West Bend property?
faqs.a: Enroll in LandNotification from Washington County, which emails you when something is recorded under your name or parcel. A recording does not automatically change ownership. If you suspect fraud, tell the police and your title insurer.
